newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus police investigate attacks on Britons.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus police investigate attacks on Britons.

text.p: Police in Cyprus said on Tuesday they were searching for a man suspected of assaulting three foreign women in the coastal resort of Paphos in the past week.

Two British holidaymakers were slightly injured in separate assaults on Monday night. The two women, who police identified as Linda Lahiff, 33, and Ellen Brooks, 45, were attacked by an unknown assailant holding a sharp instrument.
Both women sustained minor scratches to their thighs. Four days ago another foreign woman went to police with the same complaint, they said.
"This guy is a crackpot who was going around ripping up women's skirts with a blade," a police source in the capital Nicosia told Reuters.
Paphos, on the island's western coast, is a favourite for thousands of British holidaymakers where crime is rare.
Monday's assaults occurred in the space of 20 minutes as the women were walking along busy streets in the resort with their husbands.
The descriptions given of their attackers matched, police said.
A similar assault involving a foreign woman occurred four days ago, divisional police commander Andreas Nicolaides told Reuters.
"We have stepped up (security) measures and are watching the areas where the incidents took place... we hope to locate him soon," he said.
Nicolaides could not specify the assault weapon used. He said it was not a blade, but a sharp instrument.
Dozens of youths have been summoned for questioning without finding anything incriminating against them, police said.
Police could not give the home towns of the plaintiffs.
